# The own-container recipe: your agent runs in an image of yours, as a
# non-root user without sudo, and reaches the console only through its
# socket (the locklog-run volume). It never sees the logs, the keys or the
# console's terminal.
#
# 1. Add this to your agent's Dockerfile, after its packages are installed:

# locklog is not pinned by digest: pin it before you build (docker buildx imagetools inspect locklog).
# locklog's client, its root-owned system file (the console account and
# the clients group the socket admits), and the accounts it names.
COPY --from=locklog --chown=root:root --chmod=0755 /usr/local/bin/locklog /usr/local/bin/locklog
COPY --from=locklog --chown=root:root /etc/locklog/system.toml /etc/locklog/system.toml
# The console account (10051) only names the socket's owner, which the client
# checks: no shell, no home, no password, nothing runs as it here. The agent
# user is not root, has no sudo, and is in locklog-clients (10050).
RUN set -eu; \
    if command -v useradd >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
      groupadd -g 10050 locklog-clients; \
      useradd -M -N -u 10051 -s /usr/sbin/nologin locklog; \
      useradd -m -u 1000 -g locklog-clients -s /bin/sh agent; \
    else \
      addgroup -g 10050 locklog-clients; \
      adduser -D -H -u 10051 -s /sbin/nologin locklog; \
      adduser -D -u 1000 -G locklog-clients -s /bin/sh agent; \
    fi; \
    chmod 0755 /etc/locklog; chmod 0644 /etc/locklog/system.toml; \
    if command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "the agent image must not have sudo" >&2; exit 1; fi
USER 1000:10050

# 2. Start the console, in a terminal of yours, from the project:

  locklog console --profile prod --allowed-uids 1000

# 3. Run the agent's container with the socket volume and the project at its
#    own path (the socket is named after the project's path):

  docker run --rm -it -v locklog-run:/run/locklog -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" your-agent-image

# In it, the agent's MCP server is `locklog mcp` (locklog init <agent> writes the
# project's MCP entry). Every agent whose container mounts this locklog-run
# volume reaches every console on it: one locklog-run volume is one trust
# domain. Give agents that must not share a console their own volume.
# The console's image knows uid 1000 by no account: --allowed-uids 1000 admits it
# (the console's start shows it).
